title: 4. Oracle SQL filtering, joins and keys
description: Data filtering (IS NULL, BETWEEN, LIKE), table aliases, INNER / LEFT / RIGHT / FULL OUTER JOIN row analysis, and composite key matching.

items.title: Reference Scenario for Q26–35
items.content: SPORT(sportNO PK, sportNAME) has 1 swimming, 2 badminton, 3 esport, 4 spelunking, 5 pool, 6 fencing. STUDENT_SPORTENROLL(SID PK, SNAME, sportNO nullable FK) has two students in sport 1, three in sport 2 (Zack, Arthur, Hisham), three in sport 3 (including SID 23), and two with NULL (Matthew, Hafizah). SID 99 is unused. Assume joins use se.sportNO = sp.sportNO unless asked otherwise.

items.question: Which condition finds students without a sport?
items.explanation: NULL is tested with IS NULL, not equality.

items.question: Which students satisfy sportNO BETWEEN 2 AND 3?

options.text: All six in badminton and esport
The six plus the two unassigned students

items.explanation: BETWEEN includes both endpoints but does not match NULL.

items.question: Which condition finds sport names starting with lowercase s?
items.explanation: Percent matches zero or more characters; underscore matches one.

items.question: Which ON condition correctly links student alias se to sport alias sp?
items.explanation: Match the student's FK to the sport PK.

items.question: How many rows does INNER JOIN return?
What does a LEFT JOIN with students on the left return?

options.text: All ten students, with NULL sport names for two
Eight assigned students plus three unused sports

items.explanation: The left side is preserved, including unmatched students.

items.question: With students on the left, which keeps all sports but not unassigned students?
items.explanation: The right side is preserved, including unused sports.

items.question: How many rows does FULL OUTER JOIN return?
items.explanation: Eight matches, two student-only rows and three sport-only rows.

items.question: After a student-to-sport LEFT JOIN, what survives WHERE sp.sportNAME = 'badminton'?

options.text: Those three plus the two unassigned students

items.explanation: The WHERE predicate rejects NULL sport names and other sports.

items.question: Which new (SID, sportNO) can be inserted?
items.explanation: Sport 4 exists and SID 99 is unused. The other options break FK or PK rules.

items.question: Horse.sql: Which condition and join keep every ENTRY1 row while looking up its prize in PRIZE, keyed by (event_id, place)?
items.explanation: Both columns identify the prize, and unmatched entries must be preserved.
